p.src: Yinger could make neither head nor tail of Baoyu's words and was about to leave when she heard him say again, “Silly girl, let me tell you. Since your young mistress is destined for good fortune, you will naturally share in it by following her. You cannot rely on your elder sister Xiren. From now on, you need only serve your mistress with all your heart. If some benefit comes your way in the future, your years of hardship at her side will not have been in vain.” The first part of this sounded sensible to Yinger, but the latter part again seemed rather strange. “I understand,” she said. My young mistress is still waiting for me. If Second Master wants fruit, just send a little maid to fetch me.” Baoyu nodded, and only then did Yinger leave. Presently Baochai and Xiren returned and each went to her own room. No more need be said of this.

p.src: A few days later, the examination period arrived. Everyone else merely looked forward to uncle and nephew writing fine essays and winning high places, but Baochai alone noticed that, although Baoyu's studies were going well, there was an oddly detached calmness about him, whether deliberate or not. Knowing that he was about to enter the examination compound, she had two concerns. First, both uncle and nephew were sitting the examination for the first time, and she feared some mishap amid the crush of people and horses. Second, since the monk's departure Baoyu had never gone out. Though she was pleased to see him studying hard, his transformation had been so swift and so complete that she could scarcely believe it and feared some further turn of events. Thus, on the day before they entered the compound, she had Xiren take the little maids and, together with Suyun and the others, prepare everything properly for uncle and nephew. After personally inspecting it all, she had it carefully put away for the next day. She then went with Li Wan to report to Lady Wang and asked that several more mature and dependable stewards be assigned, saying only that she feared the candidates might be jostled in the crowd of people and horses.

p.src: The next day, Baoyu and Jia Lan changed into clothes that were neither quite new nor old and cheerfully came to see Lady Wang. Lady Wang admonished them: “This is the first time either of you has entered the examination compound. You have grown this old without ever being separated from me for a single day. Even when you were out of my sight, maids and married servants always surrounded you. When have you ever spent a night alone? Today you will each go inside, all alone and forlorn, with no relative in sight. You must take good care of yourselves. Finish your essays early, come out and find our servants, then return home as soon as you can, so that your mother and wife may be spared anxiety.” As she spoke, Lady Wang could not help growing sorrowful. Jia Lan assented to every injunction. Baoyu, however, uttered not a word. When Lady Wang had finished, he stepped forward and knelt before her. His eyes brimming with tears, he knocked his head three times and said, “Mother gave me life and raised me, yet I have no way to repay her. All I can do is apply myself to my essays when I enter the compound and emerge having properly earned the provincial graduate's degree. If that gives you some joy, Mother, then my life's duty as your son will be fulfilled, and all the wrong I have done throughout my life will be covered over.” These words made Lady Wang still more sorrowful. “It is naturally good that you feel this way,” she said, “but alas, your grandmother can no longer see you!” As she spoke, she took his hand to raise him. But Baoyu remained kneeling and refused to rise. “Whether Grandmother sees me or not, she will surely know and be pleased. If she knows and is pleased, then not seeing is no different from seeing. Only our bodily forms are separated; our spirits are not.” Seeing Lady Wang and Baoyu thus, Li Wan feared both that Baoyu's illness might be stirred up again and that the scene was rather inauspicious. She hurried forward and said, “Madam, this is a joyous occasion. Why be so sorrowful? Besides, Brother Baoyu has lately learned right from wrong, become most filial, and shown himself willing to study. He need only take his nephew inside, write good essays, and return early. Then we shall copy them out and ask the learned old gentlemen among our family friends to look them over, and wait until good news comes for both uncle and nephew. That will settle everything.” At the same time, she ordered the servants to help Baoyu to his feet. Baoyu turned and bowed to Li Wan. “Do not worry, Sister-in-law. Uncle and nephew are both certain to pass. Lan will achieve great distinction one day, and you, Sister-in-law, will wear the phoenix coronet and embroidered robe of honor.” “May your words come true,” Li Wan said with a smile. “Then all my—” At this point, fearing she might again arouse Lady Wang's grief, she hastily swallowed the rest. Baoyu smiled. “So long as there is a worthy son to carry on the ancestral estate, even if my elder brother cannot see it, his affairs after death may be considered complete.”

p.src: Seeing that it was growing late, Li Wan was unwilling to keep talking with him and merely nodded. By now Baochai had listened herself into a daze. Every word spoken—not only by Baoyu, but also by Lady Wang and Li Wan—seemed an ill omen. Yet she dared not take it seriously and could only hold back her tears in silence. Baoyu walked up to her and made a very deep bow. Everyone found his behavior strange and could not understand it, yet no one dared laugh at him. Then they saw tears streaming from Baochai's eyes. This astonished them still more. Then they heard Baoyu say, “Elder sister, I am leaving. Stay dutifully with Mother and await the glad news of my success.” “It is time you went,” said Baochai. “There is no need for all this rambling.” “How urgently you press me!” said Baoyu. “I know myself that it is time to go.” Turning, he saw that everyone was there except Xichun and Zijuan. “Please say a word for me to Fourth Sister and Sister Zijuan. After all, it will be enough when we meet again.” His words seemed half reasonable and half mad to them. They all concluded that, since he had never been away from home, Lady Wang's speech had stirred up this whole performance. It would be best to hurry him off and have done with it. “People are waiting for you outside,” they said. “If you keep making a fuss, you will be late.” Baoyu threw back his head and laughed loudly. “I am going, I am going! p.src: We shall say no more for now of Baoyu and Jia Lan leaving home to sit the examination. When Jia Huan saw them go off to the examination, he was filled with both anger and resentment. Thinking himself master of the house, he declared, “Now I can avenge my mother. There is not a man left in the household, and the First Lady supports me. Whom need I fear?” Having made up his mind, he hurried over to Lady Xing’s quarters, paid his respects, and plied her with flattering words. Lady Xing was naturally delighted and said, “Now you are a sensible child. In Qiaojie’s affair, I ought by rights to have the final say. Yet your Second Cousin Lian is so muddle-headed that, with the girl’s own grandmother here, he entrusts her to someone else!” Jia Huan said, “The people on the other side have said that they will recognize no match but this one. Now that it is settled, they are preparing a handsome gift for you as well. Once you have the grandson of a frontier prince as your granddaughter’s husband, can the First Master possibly fail to obtain a high office? I do not say this merely because you are my own lady, but ever since they had Imperial Consort Yuanchun, they have oppressed people beyond endurance. Qiaojie must not prove equally heartless in the future. I shall go and speak to her.” Lady Xing said, “You should tell her, so that she may learn how good you have been to her. Even if her father were at home, I doubt he could find her so fine a match! Only that foolish creature Pinger insists that the match is unsuitable and says that your lady is opposed to it too. I expect they are afraid that we shall gain the advantage. If we delay until your Second Cousin returns, he may listen to what others say, and then the marriage will never come about.” Jia Huan said, “Everything has been settled on their side. They are only waiting for you to send the slip bearing her birth data. The prince’s household has a rule that the bride must be fetched within three days. There is just one difficulty: they fear you may object. They say it would be improper to marry the granddaughter of a convicted official, so for now she can only be carried away quietly. When the First Master is pardoned and restored to office, everyone can celebrate the marriage in grand style.” Lady Xing said, “Why should I object? It is only proper according to custom.” Jia Huan said, “In that case, you need only issue the written notice.” Lady Xing said, “What a muddle-headed child you are! There are only women in these inner apartments. Just ask Cousin Yun to write one.” Jia Huan was beside himself with delight. He promptly agreed and went out, hurried to tell Jia Yun, and then took Wang Ren with him to the foreign prince’s residence to execute the agreement and collect the silver.

p.src: Little did they know that everything they had just said had been overheard by one of Lady Xing’s maids. The maid had obtained her position through Pinger’s recommendation, so she found a spare moment to hurry to Pinger and report every detail. Pinger had long known that the affair boded no good and had already explained it carefully to Qiaojie. Qiaojie had wept all night, insisting that she must wait for her father to return and decide, and that she could not obey the First Lady. Now, on hearing this latest news, she burst into loud sobs and wanted to go and reason with the lady herself. Pinger hastily stopped her. “Wait a moment, miss. The First Lady is your own grandmother. She says that in the Second Master’s absence she has the right to decide, and besides, your uncle is acting as matchmaker. They are all in league together. How could you argue against them alone? After all, I am only a servant and have no standing to speak. For now, we can only devise some plan. You must not act rashly.” Lady Xing’s maid said, “You must think of something quickly, or they will soon carry her away in the bridal chair.” With that, they each went their separate ways. Turning back, Pinger saw Qiaojie doubled up with grief. She hurried to support her and said, “Miss, crying will do no good. The Second Master is beyond our reach, and judging from what they say—” Before she could finish, someone sent by Lady Xing arrived with a message: “Wonderful news has come for the young lady. Pinger is to prepare all the young lady’s personal necessities. As for her dowry, it was agreed from the outset that it would be arranged after the Second Master returns.” Pinger had no choice but to assent.

p.src: When Pinger returned, Lady Wang had arrived. Qiaojie flung her arms around her and collapsed weeping into her embrace. Lady Wang wept too. “Do not be anxious, child. I have endured many harsh words from the First Lady on your account, but it seems I cannot bend her will. All we can do is appear to comply while delaying matters, and send a servant at once to inform your father.” Pinger said, “Have you not heard, madam? Early this morning, the Third Master told the First Lady that according to some rule of the foreign prince’s household, the girl must go there within three days. The First Lady has already ordered Cousin Yun to write out Qiaojie’s name and birth particulars and send them over. How can we wait for the Second Master?” When Lady Wang heard the words “Third Master,” she was so furious that she could not speak. After sitting stunned for a long while, she repeatedly ordered the servants to find Jia Huan. After searching for a long time, a servant reported, “He went out this morning with Cousin Qiang and Uncle Wang.” Lady Wang asked, “What about Cousin Yun?” Everyone replied that they did not know. Everyone in Qiaojie’s room stared helplessly at one another, utterly at a loss. Lady Wang could hardly quarrel openly with Lady Xing, so they could do nothing but cling to one another and weep.

p.src: An old serving woman came in and reported, “The people at the back gate say that Granny Liu has come again.” Lady Wang said, “With such trouble befalling our family, how could we have time to receive visitors? Make whatever excuse you like and send her away.” Pinger said, “Madam, you ought to let her in. She is the young lady’s godmother, so we should tell her what has happened.” Lady Wang said nothing, so the old servant brought Granny Liu in. They all exchanged greetings when they met. Granny Liu saw that everyone’s eyes were red from weeping and could make no sense of it. After hesitating a while, she asked, “What has happened? Madam and the young ladies must be missing the Second Young Mistress.” Hearing her mother mentioned, Qiaojie wept more bitterly than ever. Pinger said, “Granny, this is no time for idle talk. Since you are the young lady’s godmother, you ought to know what has happened.” She then told her the whole story in full detail. Granny Liu too was struck dumb with fright. After a long pause, she suddenly smiled and said, “For such a clever girl, haven’t you ever heard the tales sung to drum accompaniment? They are full of ways out of predicaments like this. What is so difficult about it?” Pinger hurriedly asked, “Granny, if you have a plan, tell us quickly.” Granny Liu said, “There is nothing difficult about it. Without letting a soul know, you simply slip away in a flash, and that settles everything.” Pinger said, “Now you are talking nonsense. Where could people from a family like ours possibly go?” Granny Liu said, “The only question is whether you are willing to go. If you are, come to my village. I will hide the young lady there, then have my son-in-law find someone at once. The young lady can write a note in her own hand, and the messenger can hurry to her father. He is certain to come. Would that not do nicely?” Pinger asked, “What if the Elder Madam knows about it?” Granny Liu replied, “Do they know that I have come?” Pinger said, “The Elder Madam lives in the rear quarters. She treats people harshly, so no message of any kind has been sent to her. Had you come through the front gate, she would have known, but since you entered by the back gate, there is nothing to worry about.” Granny Liu said, “Let us settle when it is to be. I will have my son-in-law hire a carriage and come to fetch you.” Pinger said, “How can we afford to wait any longer? Sit here for a moment.” She hurried inside and, taking care that no one else heard, relayed Granny Liu’s proposal. Lady Wang pondered for a long while but felt that the plan was improper. Pinger said, “This is the only way. It is only because you are here, Madam, that I dare explain it openly. You need only pretend to know nothing, and afterward you can question the Elder Madam instead. Someone from our side will go there, and I expect the Second Master will return soon as well.” Lady Wang said nothing and heaved a sigh.

You two will need clothes and bedding.” Pinger said, “The important thing is to leave quickly. If they settle the matter first, we shall be in serious trouble.” These words brought Lady Wang to her senses, and she said, “Yes, that is true. Make your preparations quickly. Seeing Jia Yun return alone, he hurried up and asked, “Is it settled?” Jia Yun stamped his foot in alarm. “This is terrible—terrible! Lady Wang rounded on Jia Huan. “A vile creature like Concubine Zhao could only leave behind a vile wretch like this!” With that, she had the maids support her back to her own room.

p.src: Jia Huan, Jia Yun, and Lady Xing began blaming one another, until one of them said, “There is no use trading accusations now. They cannot really be dead. Pinger must have taken Qiaojie into hiding at some relative’s house.” Lady Xing summoned the gatekeepers from the front and rear entrances, berated them, and demanded to know where Qiaojie and Pinger had gone. Our monthly wages and rice allowances have stopped, while they gamble, drink, frolic with young actors, and even bring women from outside into the mansion. Another messenger came from Lady Wang to press them: “Tell the gentlemen to find them quickly.” Jia Huan and the others were so frantic they wished the ground would swallow them, yet they dared not interrogate anyone from Qiaojie’s quarters. p.src: At last the day came for the candidates to leave the examination compound, and Lady Wang waited eagerly for Baoyu and Jia Lan to return. When noon came and they had still not returned, Lady Wang, Li Wan, and Baochai grew anxious and sent servants to their lodgings to inquire. One party went, but no news came back; even the messengers themselves failed to return. They sent out another party, which likewise did not return. The three women felt as though their hearts were being seared in boiling oil. At dusk someone finally entered, and they saw that it was Jia Lan. Everyone cried out joyfully, “Where is your Uncle Bao?” Without even pausing to pay his respects, Jia Lan burst into tears. “Second Uncle is missing.” Lady Wang froze at these words. For a long while she could not speak, and then she fell rigidly backward onto the bed. Fortunately Caiyun and the others were behind her and caught her. With desperate cries they finally revived her, whereupon she began to weep. Baochai too could only stare blankly, the whites of her eyes showing. Xiren and the others had already wept until they were drenched in tears. Amid her sobs, Xiren could only berate Jia Lan: “You foolish boy! You were together with your uncle—how could you let him disappear?” Jia Lan replied, “Second Uncle and I ate and slept together at our lodgings. Inside the examination compound our cells were not far apart, and we were together at every opportunity. Early this morning Second Uncle finished his paper before I did and even waited for me. The two of us handed in our papers together and came out side by side. But in the crush at the Dragon Gate, I turned around and he was gone. The men from our household who had come to meet us all asked me where he was. Li Gui said he too had seen him only a few paces away, and could not understand how he had vanished in a single press of the crowd. Li Gui and the others are searching in different directions even now. I too took men through every examination cell and searched them all, but found nothing. That is why I have only just returned.” Lady Wang wept so bitterly that she could not utter a word. Baochai had already guessed most of the truth, while Xiren sobbed without cease. Without waiting for orders, Jia Qiang and the others also set off to search in different directions. Poor inhabitants of the Rong mansion—every one of them was more dead than alive, and the food and wine prepared to welcome the candidates home went untouched. Jia Lan forgot his own exhaustion and wanted to go out searching again. But Lady Wang stopped him. “My child, your uncle is lost. Could I bear to lose you as well? Be a good boy and go get some rest.” But Jia Lan refused to leave. Lady You and the others pleaded with him repeatedly. Of all those present, only Xichun understood what had happened, though she could not very well say it aloud. She asked Baochai, “Did Second Brother take the jade with him?” “He always carries it on his person,” said Baochai. “How could he not have taken it?” Hearing this, Xichun said no more. Xiren remembered the day the jade had been snatched away and likewise suspected that the monk was behind this. Her tender heart nearly broke; pearly tears streamed down her cheeks, and she sobbed without end.

p.src: Several days passed in this way. Lady Wang wept until she could neither eat nor drink, and her life hung by a thread. Suddenly a servant came to report: “A man has arrived from the coastal frontier. He says he was sent by His Excellency the Regional Commander and that our Third Young Mistress will reach the capital tomorrow.” When Lady Wang heard that Tanchun was returning to the capital, it did not dispel her grief over Baoyu, but her heart was somewhat relieved. Seeing Lady Wang wasted and haggard, and everyone else with swollen eyes and reddened cheeks, she too burst into loud sobs. Only after weeping for some time did she perform the customary greetings. When she saw Xichun dressed as a Taoist nun, she felt deeply distressed. Then she heard that Baoyu had wandered away in a confused state and learned of the many misfortunes that had befallen the household, and they all began weeping again. Fortunately, Tanchun was eloquent and discerning. She spoke gently and consoled them for a long while, until Lady Wang and the others felt somewhat better. The day after that, the Third Son-in-law arrived as well. After learning what had happened, he let Tanchun remain there to offer comfort. The maids and married attendants who had accompanied Tanchun also gathered with their old companions, each recounting what had happened since their parting. From then on, everyone in the household, high and low, waited day and night for news of Baoyu.

p.src: One night, shortly after the fifth watch, several servants came in from outside and reached the inner gate, calling out good news. Several young maids rushed inside in such confusion that they did not even stop to tell the senior maids. Bursting into the room, they cried, “Congratulations, ladies! Wonderful news!” Lady Wang assumed that Baoyu had been found. Rising joyfully, she said, “Where did they find him? Bring him in at once!” The servant replied, “He has passed the provincial examination in seventh place.” “But where is Baoyu?” asked Lady Wang. The servant said nothing, and Lady Wang sat down again. Tanchun then asked, “Who was it that placed seventh?” The servant replied, “Second Master Bao.” While they were still speaking, another shout came from outside: “Young Master Lan has passed too!” The servant hurried out, received the official notice, and came back to report that Jia Lan had placed one hundred and thirtieth. Li Wan was delighted at heart, but since Lady Wang had not recovered Baoyu, she dared not let her joy show. Lady Wang too was pleased that Jia Lan had passed, but she could think only, “If Baoyu would just come home, how happy all of us would be!” Baochai alone was heartsick with sorrow, yet could not properly shed tears. Everyone offered congratulations, saying, “Since Baoyu was destined to pass the examination, surely he cannot remain lost. After all, who has ever heard of a provincial graduate going missing?” Lady Wang and the others thought this made sense, and faint smiles appeared on their faces. Taking advantage of the moment, everyone persuaded Lady Wang and the others to eat a little more. Just then Beiming could be heard shouting outside the third gate: “Now that our Second Master has become a provincial graduate, he can't possibly stay lost!” “How do you know that?” everyone asked. Beiming replied, “As the saying goes, ‘One triumph makes a name known throughout the realm.’ Wherever Second Master goes now, people there will know who he is. Who would dare not send him home?” Those inside all said, “The boy may have no manners, but what he says is quite right.” Xichun said, “He is a grown man. How could he simply lose his way? I fear that he has seen through the vanity of worldly life and entered the religious order. If so, it will be difficult to find him.” Her words set Lady Wang and the others weeping bitterly once more. Li Wan said, “Since ancient times, many who attained Buddhahood, became patriarchs, or achieved immortality have indeed cast aside rank and riches.” Lady Wang wept, “If he abandons his parents, that is unfilial. How could he ever attain Buddhahood or become a patriarch?” Tanchun said, “It is never good for a person to be marked by anything extraordinary. Second Brother was born with a piece of jade, and everyone called it an auspicious thing. But from this perspective, all the trouble has come from that jade. If he is still missing after a few more days—and I do not mean to distress you, Mother—there must be some deeper cause. We shall simply have to think of it as though this brother of mine had never been born. If he truly has a sacred destiny and has attained enlightenment, that too is the fruit of the merit you have cultivated over many lifetimes.”

p.src: Little did they know that Qiaojie had followed Granny Liu out of the city together with Pinger and reached the village farm. Granny Liu did not dare treat Qiaojie with the slightest disrespect; she had the best rooms cleaned and gave them to Qiaojie and Pinger for their lodging. Though their daily fare was rustic country food, it was clean and wholesome. With Qinger there to keep her company as well, Qiaojie was able to put her mind at ease for the time being. There were several wealthy households in the village. When they learned that a young lady of the Jia family had come to Granny Liu's home, every one of them came to see her, declaring her a celestial maiden descended from heaven. Some brought vegetables and fruit, while others brought game, so the place became quite lively. Among them was an exceedingly wealthy family surnamed Zhou, possessed of an immense fortune and thousands of acres of fine farmland. They had only one son, a refined and handsome boy of fourteen. His parents had engaged a tutor for his studies, and he had recently passed the local examination to become a licentiate. When his mother saw Qiaojie that day, she was filled with admiration and thought to herself, “We are only a farming family. How could we ever be worthy of a young lady from such a distinguished house?” She remained there, lost in thought. Granny Liu guessed what was on her mind, took her by the hand, and said, “I know what you are thinking. Let me arrange a match between the two families.” Madam Zhou laughed. “Do not tease me. Think what kind of family they are! Would they consent to marry their daughter into a farming household like ours?” “Let me mention it, and we shall see,” said Granny Liu. The two then went their separate ways.

p.src: Granny Liu remained concerned about the Jia household and sent Baner into the city to learn the news. When he happened to reach Ning-Rong Street that day, he saw a great many carriages and sedan chairs gathered there. Baner made inquiries nearby and was told, “The Ningguo and Rongguo houses have had their official ranks restored, and all the confiscated property has been bestowed back upon them. The family is about to rise again. Only their Baoyu has passed the examination and gained office, but no one knows where he has gone.” Delighted by the news, Baner was about to return when he saw several horses arrive and their riders dismount before the gate. The gatekeeper performed a respectful salute and said, “Second Master, you have returned! What wonderful news! Has the Elder Master recovered?” The gentleman replied with a smile, “He has recovered. And now that he has received a gracious pardon, he will soon be coming home.” He then asked, “Who are all those people?” The gatekeeper answered, “They are officials sent by His Majesty to proclaim the edict here and have the family take possession of its property.” The gentleman entered joyfully. Baner then realized that the man was Jia Lian. There was no need to inquire further, so he hurried back and told his maternal grandmother. When Granny Liu heard the news, her face lit up with joy. She went to congratulate Qiaojie and repeated everything Baner had told her. Pinger said with a smile, “Indeed! It was only thanks to what you did, Granny. Otherwise, our young lady might never have lived to see this happy day.” Qiaojie herself was more delighted than ever. While they were still talking, the man who had gone to deliver the message to Jia Lian also returned and said, “The Master, your son-in-law, was extremely grateful. He told me to bring the young lady home as soon as I arrived back. He also rewarded me with several taels of silver.” Granny Liu was highly pleased to hear this. She had two carts made ready and invited Qiaojie and Pinger to board them. Qiaojie and the others had grown accustomed to life in Granny Liu's home and now found themselves reluctant to leave. Qinger even wept, wishing desperately that she could keep them there. Granny Liu understood that Qinger could not bear to part from them, so she told the girl to accompany them into the city, and they proceeded directly to the Rongguo mansion.

p.src: Now, Jia Lian had earlier learned that Jia She was gravely ill and hurried to his place of exile. When father and son met, they wept bitterly together, after which Jia She gradually began to recover. After receiving a letter from home and learning what had happened there, Jia Lian informed Jia She and set out for home. Midway through his journey he heard of the general amnesty; after pressing on for another two days, he reached home that very day, just as the imperial decree conferring rewards arrived. Inside, Lady Xing and the others were worrying that no one was there to receive the decree. Although Jia Lan was present, he was young after all. When word came that Second Master Lian had returned, everyone greeted him with mingled sorrow and joy. There was no time then for conversation, however, and he went straight to the front hall to kneel before the imperial commissioners. They inquired after his father, then told him to report to the Imperial Household Department the next day to receive the rewards and that the Ningguo mansion would be handed over to the family for residence. The officials rose and took their leave, and Jia Lian escorted them to the gate. There he saw several country carts whose drivers the household servants were refusing to let stop, and a quarrel was under way. Jia Lian knew at once that they were the carts bringing Qiaojie back, and he cursed the servants: “You muddle-headed pack of bastards! The moment I was away, you betrayed your masters and hounded Qiaojie out of the house. Now that her rescuers have brought her back, you still try to bar their way! What grudge can you possibly bear against me?” The servants had feared that Jia Lian would not let the matter rest when he returned, but had supposed it would take him some time to discover the truth. They had not expected him to speak of it so plainly and could not understand how he knew. They could only stand there and reply, “While Second Master was away, some of us were ill and others had taken leave. Third Master, Master Qiang, and Master Yun made all the decisions; it had nothing to do with us servants.” “What damnable nonsense!” cried Jia Lian. “When I have finished my business, I shall deal with you. Bring those carts in at once!”
